title: Children, Riches, and True Greatness
overview: On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus overturns common ideas about marriage, wealth and status, and says the truly great are those who serve.

parts.label: A test about divorce (vv. 1-12)
parts.note: Religious leaders tried to trap Jesus over divorce, which the law of Moses allowed if the husband gave his wife a written notice. Jesus called that a concession to hard hearts and pointed back to creation, where marriage makes two people one, and in private he said that divorcing and remarrying counts as adultery.

parts.label: Jesus welcomes children (vv. 13-16)
parts.note: Parents brought small children for Jesus to bless, and his followers tried to send them away, which made Jesus angry. He said God's kingdom belongs to people like them, probably meaning those who receive it as a gift rather than earning it.

parts.label: The rich man's question (vv. 17-22)
parts.note: A man asked how to gain eternal life, and Jesus pointed him to the commandments about how we treat other people. Jesus loved him and asked him to give his wealth to the poor and follow him, and that was the one thing he could not do.

parts.label: The camel and the needle (vv. 23-31)
parts.note: Many people then saw wealth as a sign of God's favor, so the disciples were shocked, and the camel image is a deliberate exaggeration for something impossible by human effort but not for God. To those who had left home and family, Jesus promised a hundred times as much in this life, along with persecution, which many read as the wider family they would find among his followers, and he said the usual rankings would be turned upside down.

parts.label: Death ahead, and who is greatest (vv. 32-45)
parts.note: Jesus foretold his death and rising for the third time, and right after, James and John asked for the seats of honor beside him, not grasping that his 'cup' and 'baptism' meant suffering. He said greatness means serving, since he came to give his life as a 'ransom', the price paid to free a captive, which Christians read as the heart of why he died.

parts.label: Blind Bartimaeus sees (vv. 46-52)
parts.note: A blind beggar called Jesus 'Son of David', a title for the promised king from David's family line, and kept shouting when others told him to be quiet. Jesus asked him the same question he had just asked James and John, and this man's simple request to see, and his choice to follow, stands in quiet contrast to theirs.

disagreement: Christians genuinely differ on whether Jesus' call to give up wealth and follow him is a demand on every follower or a specific test for one man whose riches held him back.
think: Who have you known who seemed great because of how they served others rather than because of the power they held, and what made them stand out to you?
